correctness.rationale: For p not dividing n, the d-period fixed subspace has kernel size q^(gcd(d,a)+gcd(d,b)-gcd(d,a,b)); this follows from squarefree cyclic polynomial roots. Divisor Möbius inversion establishes the primitive census. Cyclotomic eigenspaces establish iff lcm(gcd(n,a),gcd(n,b))=n and the nonzero-operator dichotomy. A q-fold quotient of primitive factor pairs establishes the coprime product. Direct finite enumerations of 58,939 configurations and 110 instance comparisons passed. No finite test is used to infer an infinite assertion.

value.rationale: This natural two-scale difference family exhibits an exact nontrivial symmetry-erasure boundary: maximal spatial asymmetry can be annihilated by a nonzero map iff the semisimple circumference has at least two prime divisors. The sharp primitive count and coprime factorization quantify the rare extinction sector in an all-length reproducible way, not merely a finite example.
